answer: Require lineage-diverse juries. Every account sits on a branch of the invite tree, like trees in one orchard. A reward settles only when its graders are drawn at random from at least three branches with no shared root. A farm can plant a whole knoll of fakes under one inviter, but they all hang off the same root, so they can never form a valid jury for each other. To taste the nectar of payouts, their work must convince strangers from unrelated branches, and each extra fake adds no new branch.
